title: Cap. IV Arg. 5 Sol: Major false — temporal adoption needs faith; eternal destinatio need not
pass_a_gloss: Solution. The Major proposition is false. For although perfect temporal adoption involves faith, as an antecedent condition, or at least concurrent in the very moment of adoption; and therefore no one can be considered as actually adopted, who is not at the same time considered as faithful: yet adoption, or destination unto adoption, in the Divine mind before the foundations of the world were laid both can and ought to be considered, without consideration of faith in us as an antecedent condition.
pass_b_english: Sol. That Major fails. Yes, finished temporal adoption carries faith with it — beforehand as a condition, or at least together with adoption in the same moment — so you cannot treat someone as actually adopted without treating him as faithful. But destination unto adoption in God's mind before the world's foundations can and must be thought without treating our faith as an antecedent condition.
source_text: Sol. Major propositio falsa est. Nam quamvis perfecta adoptio temporalis involvat fidem, ut conditionem antecedentem, vel saltem in ipso momento adoptionis concurrentem; ac proinde nemo considerari possit ut actu adoptatus, qui non simul consideretur ut fidelis: tamen adoptio, vel destinatio εἰς υἱοθεσίαν in mente Divina ante jacta mundi fundamenta considerari et potest, et debet, absque consideratione fidei in nobis tanquam conditionis antecedaneae.
